profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility SEA_WESTIN, at 2001 6th Avenue, Seattle, WA 98121, known as the Westin Building Exchange, one of the Pacific Northwest's most significant carrier hotel and interconnection sites. Digital Realty's own property listing for this facility, fetched this session, lists the building at 412,500 square feet.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is Digital Realty's Seattle-metro property, a historic 1920s-era structure repurposed as a data center and carrier hotel and long recognized as a key interconnection point for Pacific Northwest and transpacific network traffic. Seattle City Light serves most of the downtown Seattle data center market. Digital Realty markets this property under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning Seattle alongside its larger West Coast hubs in Silicon Valley and Los Angeles, both tracked in this registry, within its global interconnection and colocation platform.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage; the company reports its portfolio metrics by region and metro rather than disclosing per-building IT power ratings for any of its facilities, a pattern consistent across every Digital Realty property researched this session, not specific to this building alone.

reading.body:
The Westin Building is a 412,500-square-foot colocation and carrier hotel at 2001 6th Avenue in downtown Seattle operated by Digital Realty. Digital Realty does not publish an IT megawatt rating for this building on its property page or in its financial filings, which disclose portfolio metrics by region and metro rather than per-building power capacity. Without a published figure, the building's position in AI infrastructure cannot be measured against the firm's stated capacity commitments or competing facilities.

This property ranks third by published megawatt capacity among 46 mapped data center facilities in Washington State, though that ranking reflects only two facilities statewide with disclosed power figures totaling 60 MW. The building is one of Digital Realty's smaller single-metro US footprints outside its largest hub markets in Northern Virginia, Dallas, Silicon Valley, and Chicago, where the company typically operates one to a handful of named properties rather than dense multi-building campuses. Washington State has not emerged as a primary AI infrastructure hub in Digital Realty's portfolio or across the published capacity tracked for the state.

The Westin Building's historical role as a carrier hotel and interconnection point for Pacific Northwest and transpacific network traffic positions it as a network infrastructure asset rather than a primary compute destination for AI training or inference workloads. Tenants and power allocation across the building are not published. Seattle City Light serves downtown Seattle's data center market, but grid expansion plans specific to this facility are not disclosed.
